services.name: Farm & City Centre — Gweru
services.notes: Main agro retail for Gweru and central Midlands. Strong dairy input range — Gweru is Zimbabwe's major dairy city (Dairibord HQ). Good wheat and soya input stock for commercial farms on the Gweru plateau. Irrigation equipment for vegetable production.

services.name: Windmill — Gweru Branch
services.notes: Windmill Gweru trade and retail. Bulk fertiliser depot for Midlands — delivers to Kwekwe, Shurugwi, and Gokwe on scheduled runs. Strong livestock input range for dairy and beef cattle sector.

services.name: ZFC — Gweru Depot
services.notes: ZFC fertiliser depot for Midlands. Compound D, AN 34.5%, Compound S for dryland crops. Ammonium Sulphate for tobacco (Chirumanzu area). Bulk orders for Gokwe cooperatives can be organised through this depot.

services.name: Gokwe Agro Inputs — Gokwe Town
services.notes: Gokwe is Zimbabwe's cotton heartland — the 'Cotton Triangle' of Gokwe North and South produces the majority of the country's cotton. This dealer is built around cotton inputs. Quton Bt cotton seed always in stock. Sunflower seed for rotation also important. Order soya and other inputs from Gweru — limited range in Gokwe.

services.name: Kwekwe Agro Supplier
services.address: Kwekwe Town, Robert Mugabe Way, Kwekwe
services.notes: Kwekwe is primarily a gold-mining city. Agriculture around Kwekwe includes maize, soya, and tobacco (Chirumanzu border area). Gold mine workers create demand for fresh produce — good vegetable market opportunity. Goldfields areas also have some irrigation schemes.

services.name: Nembudziya Agro Dealer — Gokwe South
services.notes: Serves Gokwe South — cotton is the dominant cash crop. Bt cotton seed through Cottco contract. Limited stock — supplement from Gokwe town for larger orders. Gokwe South is drier than Gokwe North — drought-tolerant maize important for food security.

services.name: Seed Co — Gweru Distribution
services.notes: Seed Co regional warehouse for Midlands. SC403 and SC627 maize for Region 2–3. Sunflower seed for the Gokwe rotation market. R200 soybean for Gweru commercial farms. Distributes to Gokwe and Kwekwe dealers.

services.name: GMB — Gweru Silo (Major)
services.notes: One of Zimbabwe's larger provincial silos — serves all of Midlands. Accepts maize, soya, groundnuts, sorghum, sunflower. Gweru silo handles significant volumes from Gokwe communal farmers transported here. Register seller number before harvest. Payment within 30 days.

services.name: GMB — Gokwe Collection Depot
services.notes: Key GMB depot for the Gokwe cotton belt. Accepts maize, groundnuts, sorghum, and sunflower. Cotton is sold to Cottco — not GMB. Significant volumes from Gokwe communal farmers who intercrop maize and cotton. Weighbridge available. Critical access point — distance to Gweru silo is 200+ km.

services.name: GMB — Kwekwe Collection Point
services.notes: Kwekwe GMB collection. Maize and soya accepted from commercial farms around Kwekwe. Lower volumes than Gweru. Serves as overflow collection in high-yield years.

services.name: Gweru Fresh Produce Market — Mkoba
services.notes: Main fresh produce market for Gweru — serves Zimbabwe's third-largest city. Good demand from Dairibord and other industrial workers. Gweru's altitude means cool-season vegetables (carrots, cabbage, lettuce) grow well and sell at this market. Consistent buyer presence for quality produce.

services.name: Gokwe Town Market
services.notes: Gokwe town market for the cotton belt communities. Mixed grain and produce. Maize grain, groundnuts, and sunflower sold post-harvest. Fresh produce trucked in from Gweru and grown locally along Sengwa River. Cotton community members have significant cash income post-harvest — peak buying season November–January.

services.name: Kwekwe Fresh Market
services.notes: Kwekwe market. Gold mine workers are a key market — steady income year-round. Vegetables, tomatoes, cabbages, and fruit in demand. Proximity to Gweru means competition from better-stocked Gweru produce, but local vegetables sell on freshness.

services.name: Gweru Livestock Auction — Showgrounds
services.open_hours: Monthly auction — second Friday of month; Annual Midlands Agric Show in August
services.notes: Main livestock auction for Midlands province. Beef cattle from Mberengwa and Zvishavane ranches. Dairy heifers from Gweru commercial farms. Annual Midlands Agricultural Show hosted here — important farming calendar event for the whole province.

services.name: Cottco — Gokwe Major Cotton Hub
services.open_hours: June–November Mon–Sat 07:00–18:00; Cottco office open year-round Mon–Fri 08:00–17:00
services.notes: Gokwe is Zimbabwe's most important cotton-growing area — Cottco's largest buying operation outside Kadoma HQ. The Gokwe cotton community numbers hundreds of thousands of smallholder farmers. Seed provided on credit October–November. Buying June–November. Three weighbridge stations operate simultaneously during peak. Grade S1 commands best price. Payment guaranteed within 30 days — Gokwe cotton farmers are among the most financially active smallholders in Zimbabwe.
services.quality_standard: Grade S1 — clean, dry, 28–32mm staple, moisture <14%

services.name: Cottco — Gokwe South Buying Depot
services.address: Cottco Depot, Nembudziya Growth Point, Gokwe South
services.notes: Cottco satellite depot for Gokwe South. Serves the southern portion of the Gokwe cotton belt. Seed on credit pre-season. Bt and non-Bt varieties available depending on registration. Smaller operation than Gokwe North but essential given the distances.

services.name: Dairibord Zimbabwe — Gweru Dairy Collection
services.notes: Dairibord is Zimbabwe's largest dairy company — Gweru is the main processing centre. Outgrower scheme for smallholder dairy farmers: provides guidance on pasture establishment, animal husbandry, and milk cooling. Milk collected daily from registered farmers. Gweru's cool climate is ideal for dairy production. Contact for outgrower registration and current milk price per litre.

services.name: TIMB — Gweru Tobacco Buying Station
services.notes: TIMB station for Midlands province. Primarily serves tobacco farmers in Chirumanzu, Gweru, and Kwekwe districts. Flue-cured and Burley grades accepted. Grower registration required before planting season.

services.name: AGRITEX Provincial Office — Midlands
services.notes: Provincial AGRITEX HQ for Midlands. Coordinates 8 district offices. Key contacts for cotton agronomy support in Gokwe, dairy development in Gweru, and government input scheme allocation across the province.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Chirumanzu (Mvuma)
services.notes: Chirumanzu is a productive Region 2 district with significant tobacco, maize, and cotton production. Ward officers advise on tobacco establishment and TIMB registration. Also cotton agronomy for the southern parts of the district.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Gokwe North
services.notes: The most important AGRITEX office in Midlands — Gokwe North is Zimbabwe's cotton heartland. Ward officers have deep specialist knowledge of cotton agronomy. Cottco contract registration support. Also covers sorghum and groundnut production for food security. Conservation Agriculture (CA) with tied ridges is heavily promoted in Gokwe for moisture conservation.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Gokwe South (Nembudziya)
services.address: District Agricultural Office, Nembudziya Growth Point
services.notes: Gokwe South is drier than Gokwe North — more reliance on drought-tolerant crops alongside cotton. Ward officers advise on drought-tolerant variety selection and moisture-conservation tied ridges. Food security crops (sorghum, millet, nyimo beans) are promoted alongside cotton.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Kwekwe
services.notes: Kwekwe has a mixed agricultural base alongside mining. Ward officers advise on maize, soya, and tobacco for the Chirumanzu border areas. Vegetable production for the urban mine-worker market is increasingly important.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Mberengwa
services.notes: Mberengwa is one of Zimbabwe's most drought-prone districts — Region 4, very hot and dry. Ward officers focus on drought-resilient small grains. Cotton is grown but water stress is a constant challenge. Food security through sorghum, millet, and cowpeas is the primary advisory focus.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Shurugwi
services.notes: Shurugwi is a chrome-mining area with limited arable farming. Maize and cotton for communal areas. Ward officers advise on drought-tolerant cropping given the unreliable rainfall. Close to Gweru for input access.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Zvishavane
services.notes: Zvishavane is very dry (Region 4 bordering Region 5). Nickel and asbestos mining are the economic base. Limited arable potential — ward officers focus on sorghum, communal cotton, and food security crops. Close to Mberengwa in farming character.

services.name: Mlezu Agricultural College
services.notes: Agricultural college and research facility. Trains farmers and extension officers in practical agronomy for Midlands conditions. Demonstrations of cotton, maize, and sunflower best practices. Open to visiting farmers — arrange through AGRITEX Kwekwe. Annual field day open to public.

services.name: Agribank Zimbabwe — Gweru Branch
services.notes: Agribank for Midlands province. Crop loans for maize, soya, cotton, sunflower. Cotton input loans through Cottco contract. Dairy development loans for Gweru smallholder dairy farmers. Livestock loans for Mberengwa and Zvishavane ranchers. Tobacco finance for Chirumanzu and Gweru growers.

services.name: Agribank Zimbabwe — Gokwe Branch
services.notes: Agribank Gokwe — critical for the cotton belt. Cotton input loans disbursed through Cottco contract scheme. Post-cotton income creates significant repayment capacity — Gokwe farmers are among the more reliable borrowers. Crop diversification loans also available — groundnut, sunflower, sorghum alongside cotton.
